entities.summary: Agostino Chigi was a prominent Italian banker and patron of the Renaissance, born in unknown circumstances and dying on April 20, 1520. He played a crucial role in the economic and cultural development of Florence and Italy during the 15th and 16th centuries. Chigi's patronage supported artists such as Michelangelo and Raphael, and his banking activities facilitated trade and commerce across Europe. The Chigi family's influence extended to the papacy, with Agostino's nephew, Baldassare Castiglione, serving as a cardinal. Chigi's legacy can be seen in the numerous architectural and artistic projects he commissioned, including the construction of the Church of Sant'Agnese in Agone. His impact on the Renaissance was significant, shaping the cultural and economic landscape of Italy and leaving a lasting legacy in the art and architecture of the time.
